how: We read the website of every Houston wedding photographer listed on Lazo (181 listings, 143 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: a New York elopement studio, quinceanera-first studios, family and portrait photographers, photo booth rental shops, and beach-ceremony crews. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: How do you handle a humid outdoor ceremony and a dark reception room? Ask for a full gallery from a summer wedding, not just highlights.
Is a second shooter included, and how long until the full gallery arrives?
Do you charge travel inside Texas, for example to Galveston or The Woodlands?

picks.name: Bryan Anderson Weddings
picks.blurb: Bryan Anderson spent 25-plus years on magazine editorial shoots, Houston Texans players and celebrities before turning that eye on weddings. Pricing is laid out plainly, every package includes a free engagement session and full-resolution images with reprint rights, and he covers Friendswood, League City and Galveston.

picks.name: Trevino Studios
picks.blurb: Matt Trevino shoots timeless, true-to-tone wedding photographs and makes a point of the in-between, unfiltered moments. Trevino Studios is based in Pearland and works Houston, Galveston and across Texas, with packages and pricing on a page of their own.

picks.name: Blue Media Works Photography
picks.blurb: John Squyres says he has photographed more than 800 weddings in 14 years, from Central Park in New York to backyards in Texas. Blue Media Works is in Katy, and the site lists wedding packages alongside engagement and family work.

picks.name: Boulevard Photography
picks.blurb: An even blend of documentary storytelling and editorial portraits, with direction when you need it. Boulevard Photography shot a first wedding at 16, processes every gallery in-house for consistency, and sends sneak peeks within a week.

picks.name: Genovese Ashford Studios
picks.blurb: Genovese Studios is a Houston photo and video collective founded in 2007 by Chris Genovese, working mainly in documentary photojournalism: capture things as they happen, pose as little as possible. Based in El Lago, covering Houston, Galveston and Louisiana.

picks.name: Min Photography Studio - Houston Wedding Photographer
picks.blurb: Min has photographed weddings for ten-plus years and shoots documentary-first, staying close but out of the way. The site leads with a point most galleries skip: they look beautiful until the sun goes down, so ask to see the reception frames.

picks.name: Good Omen Photo & Films
picks.blurb: Val and JB are a married photo and film team in Cypress working in a documentary style with an editorial edge, Super 8 included. Good Omen prints its collections, from $4,900 at our read, and reserves space for just one featured wedding film per date.

picks.name: Eric & Jenn Photography
picks.blurb: Eric and Jenn are high school sweethearts who met in sixth-period art class and have photographed weddings together for over ten years, in a romantic style built on the small everyday moments. Based in Richmond.

picks.name: Covenant Pictures
picks.blurb: Melvin started his wedding photography career in Los Angeles and has specialized in weddings and engagements since 2011, with over 300 weddings behind him. Covenant Pictures is now based in Cypress and travels to San Antonio, Austin and Dallas.

picks.name: Exquisite Wedding Photo & Video
picks.blurb: Over a decade of wedding photography and cinematic films, honestly priced, in the studio's own words. Exquisite in Cypress includes a consultation, free travel anywhere in Texas and a full print and copyright release in every package, with no hidden fees.

picks.name: Flash Forward Productions + Media
picks.blurb: Flash Forward Productions has photographed and filmed over 1,000 weddings since 2009 from its Houston-Galveston base in Santa Fe. Collections are customizable, combination photo-and-video packages are listed, and the company is named after the owners' Goldendoodle.

picks.name: Ryan R Jones Wedding Photography
picks.blurb: Ryan R. Jones started in photography developing film in a lab over 20 years ago, then served as a Navy diver in Hawaii, where he began shooting weddings. Now based in Galveston, with a timeless, portrait-led style, and destination weddings on offer.
